title: Bear and Elections
statementMd:
Limak is a grizzly bear who desires power and adoration. He wants to win in upcoming elections and rule over the Bearland.

There are $*n*$ candidates, including Limak. We know how many citizens are going to vote for each candidate. Now $*i*$-th candidate would get $*a*_{*i*}$ votes. Limak is candidate number $1$. To win in elections, he must get strictly more votes than any other candidate.

Victory is more important than everything else so Limak decided to cheat. He will steal votes from his opponents by bribing some citizens. To bribe a citizen, Limak must give him or her one candy - citizens are bears and bears like candies. Limak doesn't have many candies and wonders - how many citizens does he have to bribe?

## Input

The first line contains single integer $*n*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$) - number of candidates.

The second line contains $*n*$ space-separated integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 1000$) - number of votes for each candidate. Limak is candidate number $1$.

Note that after bribing number of votes for some candidate might be zero or might be greater than $1000$.

## Output

Print the minimum number of citizens Limak must bribe to have strictly more votes than any other candidate.

## Note

In the first sample Limak has $5$ votes. One of the ways to achieve victory is to bribe $4$ citizens who want to vote for the third candidate. Then numbers of votes would be $9, 1, 7, 2, 8$ (Limak would have $9$ votes). Alternatively, Limak could steal only $3$ votes from the third candidate and $1$ vote from the second candidate to get situation $9, 0, 8, 2, 8$.

In the second sample Limak will steal $2$ votes from each candidate. Situation will be $7, 6, 6, 6$.

In the third sample Limak is a winner without bribing any citizen.
statementZhMd:
Limak 是一只渴望权力与崇拜的灰熊。他想在即将举行的选举中获胜，并统治 Bearland。

共有 $*n*$ 名候选人，其中包括 Limak。我们知道每位候选人将获得的选票数。现在第 $*i*$ 位候选人将获得 $*a*_{*i*}$ 张选票。Limak 是 1 号候选人。为了赢得选举，他必须获得严格多于其他任何候选人的选票。

胜利比一切都重要，因此 Limak 决定作弊。他会通过贿赂一些选民，从竞争对手那里窃取选票。为了贿赂一名选民，Limak 必须给他或她一颗糖果——选民都是熊，而熊喜欢糖果。Limak 没有很多糖果，他想知道：他至少需要贿赂多少名选民？

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$）——候选人的数量。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $*a*_{*1*}, *a*_{*2*}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 1000$）——每位候选人的选票数。Limak 是 1 号候选人。

注意，贿赂后，某位候选人的选票数可能为零，也可能大于 $1000$。

## 输出格式

输出 Limak 为了获得严格多于其他任何候选人的选票，至少需要贿赂的选民数量。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，Limak 有 $5$ 张选票。一种获胜的方法是贿赂 4 名想要投给第三位候选人的选民。这样各候选人的选票数将变为 $9, 1, 7, 2, 8$（Limak 将拥有 $9$ 张选票）。另一种方法是只从第三位候选人那里窃取 $3$ 张选票，再从第二位候选人那里窃取 $1$ 张选票，得到 $9, 0, 8, 2, 8$ 的结果。

在第二个样例中，Limak 将从每位候选人那里窃取 $2$ 张选票。结果将为 $7, 6, 6, 6$。

在第三个样例中，Limak 无需贿赂任何选民就已经是获胜者。
